subject: Agriculture
title: The Dust Bowl Locust Plagues
description: A 60-second lesson on The Dust Bowl Locust Plagues.

hook.text: In the 1870s, Rocky Mountain locusts formed swarms covering 510,000 km²—larger than California. Then they went extinct.

buildup.text: The swarm of 1875 contained an estimated 12.5 trillion insects—the largest animal aggregation ever recorded.

discovery.text: Locusts ate everything—crops, leather harnesses, wooden fence posts, and the clothes off people's backs.

twist.text: By 1902, the Rocky Mountain locust was extinct. Farmers had plowed up its breeding habitat in river valleys.

climax.text: The extinction was accidental—no one planned it. Habitat destruction solved a pest problem no one could otherwise stop.

punchline.text: Humanity's worst locust plague was accidentally eliminated by farming itself.

quiz.question: Why did the Rocky Mountain locust go extinct?
options: Farmers unknowingly plowed up its breeding habitat in river valleys
